home-remodeling.hero_sub: Full-gut renovations for oceanfront estates and Intracoastal-side homes along Hillsboro Mile, permitted through the Town of Hillsboro Beach, inspected at every stage, and run day to day by a licensed general contractor, Lic. CGC1539072.
home-remodeling.local_heading: One road, two shorelines, zero shortcuts
intro_paragraphs: Hillsboro Beach is three and a bit miles of barrier island with a single road down the middle, and fewer than two thousand residents on the last census. The housing splits cleanly: low-rise oceanfront condominiums like Hillsboro Island House, Opal Towers and the Sea Club, and the estate lots of Hillsboro Mile that run from the sand across A1A to a private dock on the Intracoastal. Most of that stock went up between the 1950s and the 1980s. Owners here rarely want a different house. They want this one, gutted to the block and rebuilt around modern mechanical systems.

The Town of Hillsboro Beach Building Department reviews and permits the work, enforcing the codes adopted by the Florida Building Commission and administered by the Broward County Board of Rules and Appeals. Broward sits inside the High-Velocity Hurricane Zone, so every window, door and roof assembly needs a product approval valid for HVHZ conditions. Add the town's turtle-lighting ordinance, which limits ocean-facing glass to a light transmittance of forty-five percent or less, and your impact glass has two specifications to satisfy instead of one. Flood elevation and the fifty-percent substantial-improvement threshold shape anything close to a full gut.

Behind the estimate sit twenty-plus years of South Florida building and more than 150 remodels and additions, all permitted and inspected. On a street this narrow, how a crew behaves matters as much as what it builds: deliveries scheduled so A1A keeps moving, a tidy site at the end of every day, and a supervisor on the job rather than on the phone. Your scope is fixed in writing before demolition. One team carries the work from estimate through final inspection and warranty, which means one number to call and nobody to blame but us.
home-remodeling.scope_intro: Every line is written and priced before a wall comes down. Here is what a Hillsboro Mile whole-home remodel usually involves.

scope_items.name: Layout, opened up
scope_items.desc: Removing interior walls between kitchen, dining and living space, with engineered beams and sealed calculations where a 1960s block house needs the help.

scope_items.name: Impact glass, twice specified
scope_items.desc: Openings replaced with units approved for High-Velocity Hurricane Zone pressures and, on ocean elevations, tinted to meet the town's sea turtle transmittance limit.

scope_items.name: Systems replaced end to end
scope_items.desc: New panels and service, repiped supply and drainage, and ducted air handling sized for a house that sits in salt air year round.

scope_items.name: Salt-air exterior envelope
scope_items.desc: Stucco repair, coatings, flashing and roof coordination chosen for an oceanfront exposure that eats ordinary hardware in a handful of seasons.

scope_items.name: Wet rooms, done in order
scope_items.desc: Both trades folded into the master permit so waterproofing, stone and cabinetry happen once, in order, instead of as three separate small projects.

faqs.q: Who issues building permits in Hillsboro Beach?
faqs.a: The Town of Hillsboro Beach runs its own Building Department out of Town Hall on Hillsboro Mile. Plan review, permits and inspections all happen at the town level, under codes adopted by the Florida Building Commission and administered county-wide by the Broward County Board of Rules and Appeals. That last part matters more than it sounds: the county certifies the building officials and inspectors and sets the administration standards every municipality here works within.

faqs.q: My house is in a flood zone. What is the fifty percent rule?
faqs.a: If the cost of improvement or repair reaches half the market value of the structure, the building is treated as substantially improved and has to be brought up to current floodplain, zoning and building standards, which usually means elevating the finished floor above base flood elevation. On a barrier island that is a design decision, not a footnote. We price the work and the appraisal question early so you choose the scope deliberately.

faqs.q: Is living here during a whole-home remodel realistic?
faqs.a: During a true gut, no, and we would rather say that in the first meeting than in month three. Ceilings come down, water goes off, and the air conditioning follows. Many Hillsboro Beach owners are seasonal anyway, which makes this town unusually easy to schedule around: we take the heavy demolition and rough-in phases in the off months and aim to have you back for finish selections and walk-throughs.

faqs.q: Why does my new glass have to be tinted?
faqs.a: Because Hillsboro Beach protects nesting sea turtles, and the town's lighting ordinance limits how much interior light escapes toward the beach during nesting season. Ocean-facing glass is expected to hold a light transmittance of forty-five percent or less, or interior light must be shielded after nine at night. Combine that with HVHZ impact requirements and you get a fairly narrow product list. We specify from it at design stage rather than at the window order.

faqs.q: What does a whole-home remodel run on Hillsboro Mile?
faqs.a: Wide, and honestly so. A cosmetic refresh of a two-bedroom condominium and a block-to-block rebuild of an ocean-to-Intracoastal estate are not the same species of project. What we commit to is a fixed written scope with real allowances, so the number you sign is the number you pay unless something genuinely unforeseen turns up and gets documented. PGX competes on certainty and finish quality. If low bid is the deciding factor, we will say so early.

home-remodeling.cta_sub: Bring the survey, the wish list, or just the frustration. You get a straight read and a written scope, in English o en español.

kitchen-remodeling.title: Kitchen Remodeling, Hillsboro Beach FL | PGX Builders Group
kitchen-remodeling.meta_description: Custom kitchen remodeling in Hillsboro Beach, FL — condo stack constraints, estate islands, permits and inspections handled. Talk to PGX: (786) 273-2524.
kitchen-remodeling.h1: Kitchens built for a barrier island
kitchen-remodeling.hero_sub: Custom cabinetry, stone counters and layout changes for Hillsboro Beach condominiums and estate homes, permitted through the town, coordinated with your association, and supervised on site every working day.
intro_paragraphs: Two kitchen problems dominate Hillsboro Beach, and they are almost opposites. In the low-rise buildings, places like Port de Mer, Kingsley Arms and Hillsboro Windsor, you are working inside a footprint drawn decades ago, with plumbing stacks and structural slabs that decide where the sink can go. In the estate houses along Hillsboro Mile, the constraint is scale: a room built for a caterer's staff now has to hold an island, a wine wall, and everyone who wandered in from the dock. Different puzzles, same answer, which is measuring before promising.

Because a kitchen at this level touches plumbing, electrical and often structure, it gets permitted through the Town of Hillsboro Beach Building Department and inspected before anything is closed up. In a condominium, the association comes first: approval of the plans, proof of insurance, and a slot on the service elevator, which in a small building is a genuinely scarce resource. Buildings of three habitable stories or more are also working through Florida's milestone inspection and structural reserve study requirements, which can affect when a board is willing to sign off on unit work.

We build kitchens in the sequence that keeps them intact. Cabinets get ordered early because good millwork takes months, stone is templated after the boxes are set rather than off a drawing, and appliances are confirmed against real rough-in dimensions before a wall closes. Floors, corridors and elevator cabs are protected on the way in and out. You get a fixed written price, a daily supervisor, and crews who understand that in a building where half the owners are away, the neighbors who stayed deserve quiet afternoons.
kitchen-remodeling.scope_heading: The pieces of an island kitchen
kitchen-remodeling.scope_intro: Priced line by line before anything is demolished. The five items below cover most of what a Hillsboro Beach kitchen actually needs.

scope_items.name: Cabinetry made to fit
scope_items.desc: Boxes built for salt-air humidity, scribed to walls that are rarely square, and drawn to the ceiling height you have rather than the one a catalog assumes.

scope_items.name: Stone, templated in place
scope_items.desc: Marble, quartzite or porcelain slabs templated after cabinets are installed, with island framing engineered to carry the weight and the seating overhang.

scope_items.name: Moving the plumbing wall
scope_items.desc: Relocating sinks and dishwashers within what the slab and the building's existing stacks will allow, verified before design instead of discovered during demolition.

scope_items.name: Appliances and their infrastructure
scope_items.desc: Dedicated circuits, upgraded panels, water lines and exhaust routed and permitted so the range, the wine storage and the ice maker all work at once.

scope_items.name: Light you can cook under
scope_items.desc: Layered ceiling, task and cabinet lighting on proper controls, replacing the single fixture that has been doing all the work since the building opened.

faqs.q: Will my condo association let me remodel the kitchen?
faqs.a: Almost always, on their terms. Expect to submit plans, name your contractor, provide a certificate of insurance listing the association, and agree to working hours and an elevator schedule. Some Hillsboro Beach boards also want an engineer's letter before any slab penetration. We assemble that package as part of the job, because a board that gets a complete submittal on the first pass approves faster than one that gets three emails.

faqs.q: Can I move the sink and range in a condominium unit?
faqs.a: Sometimes, within limits. Drainage has to reach the building's existing stack at a workable slope, and in older Hillsboro Beach buildings that stack is where it is. On a concrete slab, cutting or coring for new drain lines is engineering work and usually needs association and structural sign-off. Ranges may be limited by ventilation paths. We survey the mechanical reality first and design the kitchen to the plumbing rather than the other way around.

faqs.q: How long is the kitchen out of service?
faqs.a: Plan on a couple of months of site work for a full kitchen, longer when walls move or a panel needs upgrading. The longer clock is fabrication: custom cabinetry commonly runs three to four months from approved shop drawings, so we order first and demolish later. That sequencing is the whole trick. Nobody should be washing dishes in a bathtub while a factory in another state gets around to their doors.

faqs.q: Does salt air really affect kitchen finishes?
faqs.a: Indoors it is subtler than on a terrace, but yes. Buildings this close to the Atlantic run humid, and doors get left open. We specify hardware and hinges rated for coastal environments, finishes that tolerate moisture cycling, and honest ventilation so cooking humidity leaves the room instead of settling into cabinet boxes. On ocean-facing units we also check that new glazing near the kitchen still satisfies the town's turtle-lighting transmittance rule.

faqs.q: What should a high-end kitchen here cost?
faqs.a: Cabinetry, stone and appliances set the budget, and those are selections, not square footage. A galley refresh in a two-bedroom unit and a full estate kitchen with a scullery sit in genuinely different brackets. We would rather scope precisely than quote a per-foot fantasy, so after a walk-through you get a written specification with a fixed number attached. We are a high-end builder and priced accordingly, which some people find refreshing and others find disqualifying.

kitchen-remodeling.cta_sub: A walk-through, a measured plan, and a fixed written estimate for the kitchen. We work in English o en español, whichever is easier.

bathroom-remodeling.title: Bathroom Remodels for Hillsboro Beach, FL | PGX Builders
bathroom-remodeling.meta_description: Primary bath and guest bath remodels in Hillsboro Beach — flood-tested waterproofing, frameless glass, stone, and permits pulled. Call (786) 273-2524.
bathroom-remodeling.hero_sub: Primary suites, frameless showers and freestanding tubs for Hillsboro Beach homes and condominiums, with waterproofing flood-tested before tile, permits pulled through the town, and a licensed general contractor accountable for every inspection.
intro_paragraphs: The bathrooms in Hillsboro Beach were mostly built for a different decade of expectations. Oceanfront units in buildings like Hillsboro Island House, Opal Towers and the Sea Club came with compact baths and a single vanity, and the estate houses on Hillsboro Mile tend to have plenty of bathrooms and not one primary suite anyone would design today. So the projects here are conversions as much as renovations: absorbing a closet or a small bedroom, replacing a tub nobody uses with a shower two people can stand in, and finishing it in stone that will survive the salt.

Bathroom work is permitted through the Town of Hillsboro Beach Building Department, with plumbing, electrical and mechanical inspections along the way, all under the Florida Building Code as administered by the Broward County Board of Rules and Appeals. In a condominium, add association approval, a certificate of insurance and agreed working hours. The buildings themselves are the bigger variable: original cast iron waste lines, galvanized supply, and post-tensioned or conventionally reinforced slabs that decide whether a curbless shower is possible or merely photogenic. We investigate that before design, not during demolition.

Everything that matters in a bathroom is buried by the time you see it, which is why we build the invisible half first. Waterproofing membranes are flood-tested and held overnight before tile is set. Shower slopes are checked with instruments. Blocking for heavy glass goes into the wall months before the glass arrives. The rest of your home is already finished, so it gets covered and protected from the front door in. Fixed written scope, a supervisor here daily, licensed and insured under Lic. CGC1539072.
bathroom-remodeling.scope_heading: The pieces of an island bath
bathroom-remodeling.scope_intro: Written down and priced before the tile order goes in. These five elements carry most Hillsboro Beach bathroom projects, whether estate house or oceanfront unit.

scope_items.name: Primary suites, assembled
scope_items.desc: Borrowing a closet, a hall or a small bedroom to build the double vanity, water closet and dressing space the original plan never allowed for.

scope_items.name: Showers with tested pans
scope_items.desc: Sloped pans and membranes flood-tested before any tile is set, linear drains where the layout wants them, and frameless panels anchored into purpose-built structure.

scope_items.name: Old pipe, replaced now
scope_items.desc: Swapping cast iron waste and galvanized supply while the walls are already open, which is the least expensive hour that work will ever cost.

scope_items.name: Stone and salt air
scope_items.desc: Marble, travertine and porcelain selected and sealed for coastal humidity, with fixtures and hardware finished to resist what the Atlantic does to chrome.

scope_items.name: Ventilation that actually vents
scope_items.desc: Salt-air rated fans on a short, real duct run to the outside, sconces flanking the mirror, and switching that separates shower from vanity.

faqs.q: Is a permit required if I am only replacing the shower?
faqs.a: If the shower is being reframed, repiped, rewaterproofed or moved, yes. Replacing a valve trim or a shower door is maintenance; rebuilding a pan is regulated work with rough plumbing and waterproofing inspections attached. The Town of Hillsboro Beach permits and inspects it, and the inspection record is worth having. Unpermitted bath work has an unpleasant habit of resurfacing during a sale or an insurance claim.

faqs.q: Can I get a curbless shower in a condominium unit?
faqs.a: It depends on the slab, and nobody should promise before looking. Recessing a pan means removing concrete, which in a post-tensioned slab is a serious engineering conversation and in some buildings simply is not permitted. Where the structure will not cooperate, a very low curb with a properly sloped pan gets you most of the look and all of the performance. We get the building's structural drawings and the association's position before you commit to a rendering.

faqs.q: My building is going through milestone inspections. Should I wait?
faqs.a: Usually not, but ask the board what is coming. Milestone inspections and structural reserve studies apply to buildings of three habitable stories or more, and if your building is scheduled for balcony or structural repairs on your stack, sequencing your interior work around that is simply sensible. Sometimes the smart move is to finish your bath first so the finished surfaces are protected during the building's work. We will read the board's schedule with you.

faqs.q: Why does the plumbing keep coming up in your estimates?
faqs.a: Because in houses and buildings from the 1950s through the 1970s, the drain and supply lines are frequently at the end of their service life, and a new stone bathroom draining into a failing stack is an expensive way to postpone a problem. We camera the lines during the estimate so the decision is made on evidence. If the pipe is sound, we say so and leave it alone.

faqs.q: What does a primary bathroom cost at this level?
faqs.a: Stone, glass and fixtures are visible drivers; the drains, supply, waterproofing and ventilation behind them are the part owners underestimate. Two bathrooms of identical size can differ by a wide margin depending on whether the building cooperates. Rather than publish a range that means nothing for your unit, we walk the space, scope what it actually needs and issue a fixed written number. We compete on finish quality and certainty, not on being the cheapest of three.

bathroom-remodeling.cta_sub: Show us the room, the plumbing and the ambition. You get a real scope and a real number, in English o en español.

home-additions.title: Hillsboro Beach, FL Home Additions | PGX Builders
home-additions.meta_description: Additions and extensions in Hillsboro Beach, FL — town commission site plan review, dune setbacks, CCCL and flood elevation handled. PGX: (786) 273-2524.
home-additions.h1: Adding square footage where land is scarce
home-additions.hero_sub: Rear extensions, second stories and garage conversions in Hillsboro Beach, engineered for coastal wind and flood elevation, taken through town site plan review and permitting, and built by one licensed, insured team.
home-additions.local_heading: Growing a house between two waters
intro_paragraphs: Land is the scarce thing in Hillsboro Beach. The town holds roughly a third of a square mile of dry ground, strung along one road, and nobody is making more of it. So owners on Hillsboro Mile expand what they have: a rear wing toward the Intracoastal, a second floor over a low 1960s ranch, a garage turned into a guest suite, a conditioned room where a screened porch has been slowly losing its argument with the salt. Estate lots that run from the beach across A1A to a private dock have room in the middle. Most of the work happens there.

Additions here are a zoning exercise before they are a construction one. The Town of Hillsboro Beach reviews site plans at the commission level, and a complete set of drawings is expected two months ahead of the meeting it is calendared for. The code caps most buildings at three stories and thirty-five feet, measured above average dune elevation east of A1A and above the crown of the road on the west side, and holds an 85-foot front setback. Runoff has to stay off A1A, mechanical equipment has to be screened, and oceanward work can fall under the state's coastal construction control line.

Experience on an addition either shows or is conspicuously absent. Tying a new foundation to a fifty-year-old one, matching stucco texture and roof profile so the seam disappears, keeping the occupied half of the house livable and clean while the other half is open to the sky. PGX has delivered more than 150 remodels and additions across South Florida, every one permitted and inspected. We fix the scope in writing, we run the site daily, and we carry the project from the first feasibility conversation through final inspection and warranty without handing you off.
home-additions.scope_heading: Where an oceanfront lot has room
home-additions.scope_intro: Every one of these starts with a survey, a structural opinion and a clear read of what the town will approve. Then we draw.

scope_items.name: Building toward the Intracoastal
scope_items.desc: Family rooms and primary suites extended toward the Intracoastal side, with footings, beams and the roof connection drawn as a single engineered package.

scope_items.name: Second floors, structure first
scope_items.desc: An engineer evaluates existing block, footings and tie beams before anything is drawn, then the upper floor is designed to the three-story cap the code allows.

scope_items.name: Converting the garage properly
scope_items.desc: Bringing garage and covered space into the conditioned envelope with insulation, impact openings and permitted mechanical work an appraiser can count.

scope_items.name: Guest and staff suites
scope_items.desc: Private quarters with a shower bath and small galley for visiting family or house staff, scaled to the architecture rather than bolted onto the back of it.

scope_items.name: Elevation and flood work
scope_items.desc: Raising finished floor, reworking foundations and detailing flood openings where base flood elevation or a substantial improvement determination puts the house into current standards.

faqs.q: Does my addition have to go before the Town Commission?
faqs.a: If it needs site plan approval, yes. Hillsboro Beach runs site plan review and its Board of Zoning Appeals through the Town Commission itself, and complete, coordinated drawings are expected roughly two months ahead of the meeting. Survey, civil, landscape and architectural sheets all have to agree, with a signed coordination letter from the consultants. It is a small town with a serious process. We build that lead time into the schedule from day one.

faqs.q: How tall can I build on Hillsboro Mile?
faqs.a: Less tall than most people assume. The code holds most of the Mile to three stories and thirty-five feet, measured above average dune elevation on the ocean side of A1A and above the crown of the road on the Intracoastal side, with that dune elevation established on your survey. Decorative features such as cupolas and railings can add a limited amount above the cap. Variances exist, but they are heard by a Board of Zoning Appeals made up of the Town Commission, and the hardship standard is not a formality.

faqs.q: Can I build toward the beach?
faqs.a: Rarely as far as you would like. Construction seaward of Florida's coastal construction control line needs a permit from the state Department of Environmental Protection, the dune and its vegetation are protected, and the town's plans have to show an easterly building line that structures respect. Practically, that pushes most additions toward the road or the Intracoastal side of the property. We map the control line, the dune elevation and the setbacks onto your survey before anyone sketches a room with an ocean view.

faqs.q: How long does an addition take here?
faqs.a: Front-load your patience. Design, structural engineering, site plan review and permitting commonly consume several months before ground breaks, and the town's submittal calendar sets part of that pace. Construction then runs several more months depending on size, elevation work and whether a second story is involved. Twelve months between the first conversation and furniture in the new room is not a pessimistic estimate for a substantial addition; it is the normal one. You get the full timeline in writing, with the review milestones named.

faqs.q: Is adding on worth it, or should I rebuild?
faqs.a: On this island, the arithmetic is unusual. Lots are effectively unrepeatable, and the flood rules mean that once your investment crosses the substantial improvement threshold, the whole structure has to meet current standards anyway. Sometimes that tips the answer toward a full rebuild; often it does not, especially when a house sits at a workable elevation. We run that analysis with real numbers before you commission drawings, and we tell you when the honest answer is not the one that gives us more work.

home-additions.cta_sub: Send the survey and describe the room you are missing. You get a feasibility read, the review path, and honest numbers, in English o en español.

outdoor-living.title: Hillsboro Beach FL Outdoor Living | PGX Builders Group
outdoor-living.meta_description: Pool decks, summer kitchens, dune crossovers and seawall coordination in Hillsboro Beach, FL. Turtle-safe lighting, permits, engineering. Call (786) 273-2524.
outdoor-living.h1: Outdoor rooms between dune and dock
outdoor-living.hero_sub: Terraces, summer kitchens, pergolas, driveways and dock-side decks for Hillsboro Beach properties, engineered for wind and salt, permitted through the town and the agencies that govern the shoreline.
intro_paragraphs: An ocean-to-Intracoastal property in Hillsboro Beach is really two outdoor projects wearing one address. On the Atlantic side there is a dune, a beach walkover and whatever terrace the code and the control line will allow. On the Intracoastal side there is a seawall, a dock, a lift and the shaded terrace where people actually sit. Owners at Hillsboro Mile Ocean Club or Royal Flamingo Villas have a narrower version of the same problem: a balcony or patio that faces salt spray and needs to be built for it.

In Hillsboro Beach, a backyard project collects agencies. The town permits the structures and reviews the site plan, with rules covering pool deck setbacks, site walls held back from the A1A pavement, gate column heights, screened mechanical equipment and driveway runoff that must be kept off the state road rather than sheeted onto it. Beach access structures have to respect the easterly building line and the dune shown on your survey. Seawalls and docks pull in county environmental review and, depending on the work, state and federal approvals; Broward's resiliency standards are also raising minimum seawall elevations over the coming decades. Lighting follows the turtle ordinance.

Exterior work at PGX gets the same discipline as interior work, which is not universal in this trade. Utilities for a summer kitchen are permitted and inspected, not run and buried. Pergola footings are engineered for the wind loads the High-Velocity Hurricane Zone requires. Terraces are pitched so water leaves the house instead of collecting against it. Fixtures on the ocean side are specified at the color temperature and shielding the turtle ordinance calls for. Fixed written scope, daily supervision, a clean site every evening, and a crew that keeps the one road passable.
outdoor-living.scope_heading: What we build outside the walls
outdoor-living.scope_intro: One terrace or both shorelines of the same property, it is drawn, permitted and built as a single job with one schedule.

scope_items.name: Summer kitchens that survive
scope_items.desc: Marine-grade stainless, sealed dense stone and coastal-rated hardware, with gas, water and electrical runs permitted and inspected rather than improvised on a weekend.

scope_items.name: Pergolas and covered terraces
scope_items.desc: Shade structures with engineered footings and hurricane-rated connections, detailed to the lines of the house instead of ordered from a catalogue of one size.

scope_items.name: Beach walkovers and decks
scope_items.desc: Boardwalks and beach access structures set behind the easterly building line, detailed to protect the dune vegetation that holds the sand in place.

scope_items.name: Seawalls, docks and terraces
scope_items.desc: Coordinating shoreline work and the deck above it, including county environmental review, so the finished terrace and the structure under it are one project.

scope_items.name: Turtle-compliant exterior lighting
scope_items.desc: Shielded, low-mounted, long-wavelength fixtures and ocean-facing glazing chosen to meet the town's nesting-season limits, because a lighting violation is a very avoidable letter.

faqs.q: How many approvals does a backyard project actually need?
faqs.a: More than a backyard project sounds like it should. The structure gets a building permit, the gas, water and electrical runs get their own trade permits, and anything that changes site conditions may need site plan review at the town, where a complete set is due two months before the commission meeting. Push toward the dune or the water and you add Broward County, sometimes the state, occasionally the Army Corps. We assemble and track the whole stack so you are not learning agency acronyms at dinner.

faqs.q: Can I put lights around the pool during turtle season?
faqs.a: Yes, if they are the right lights. The town's ordinance bars lighting that directly illuminates the beach from sunset to sunup during nesting season, March 1 through October 31, and the practical fixes are long-wavelength lamps, shielding, and mounting low enough that the source is not visible from the sand. Ocean-facing glass carries a 45 percent transmittance limit as well. We design the lighting plan to those rules rather than retrofitting it after a nighttime inspection.

faqs.q: My seawall is old. Do I have to raise it?
faqs.a: Possibly, and the direction of travel is clear. Broward County has adopted resiliency standards that phase in higher minimum seawall elevations over the next couple of decades, applied to new construction and major rehabilitation, and coastal cities are aligning their codes with them. If your dock and terrace are due for work anyway, doing the seawall in the same permit and mobilization is usually cheaper than doing it twice. We will get a marine engineer's read before recommending anything.

faqs.q: What holds up outdoors on an oceanfront lot?
faqs.a: Very little that comes from a big-box aisle. Between salt spray, ultraviolet load and constant humidity, ordinary stainless pits, powder coat chalks, and cheap outdoor cabinetry swells within a couple of seasons. We specify marine-grade metals, sealed dense stone, coated fasteners chosen for coastal exposure and finishes that can be maintained rather than replaced. It costs more at selection and considerably less over ten years, which is the arithmetic most Hillsboro Beach owners are already running.

faqs.q: What should I budget for a full outdoor project?
faqs.a: It scales with utilities, structure and shoreline. A resurfaced pool deck is one order of magnitude; a covered outdoor room with a summer kitchen, gas, water, drainage and a rebuilt dock-side terrace is another entirely, before anyone mentions the seawall. Selections move the number as much as square footage does. After a site walk you get a written specification and a fixed price, which is a slower way to quote and a much less eventful way to build.

outdoor-living.cta_sub: Meet us on the property, ocean side and waterway side both. We scope it in writing, price it once, in English o en español.

permitting-compliance.h1: A clean record on the Mile
permitting-compliance.hero_sub: Permit applications, HVHZ and turtle-compliant product approvals, staged inspections, and open permits cleared before they stall a closing, filed with the Town of Hillsboro Beach Building Department by a licensed general contractor, Lic. CGC1539072.
intro_paragraphs: Most permitting calls out of Hillsboro Beach arrive with a date attached. A lien search on a Hillsboro Mile estate turns up a reroof permit from the nineties that never got its final. A dock on the Intracoastal side was rebuilt one summer while the owners were north. A unit at Port de Mer had its kitchen relocated with the association's blessing and nobody else's. A town of seasonal owners on a single road has always made quiet work easy, and the record catches up at the least convenient moment. The other half of these calls come from owners who simply want the next project filed correctly.

The permit is a Town of Hillsboro Beach matter. Its Building Department reviews the plans and inspects the work from Town Hall on the Mile, with applications and contractor registration handled through the town's online permitting portal. Behind the town sits a county layer worth knowing: the Broward County Board of Rules and Appeals publishes the county amendments to the Florida Building Code, certifies the officials and inspectors who will handle your job, and issues the interpretations that settle code arguments. All of Broward is High-Velocity Hurricane Zone, so glass, doors and roofing need HVHZ approvals, and ocean-facing openings answer to the town's sea turtle standards too.

PGX Builders Group signs as the licensed general contractor, Lic. CGC1539072, which means the liability travels with the application instead of staying with you. We retain the architect, engineer or surveyor a complete submittal actually requires, answer plan review comments in one round rather than three, and send a supervisor to meet the inspector instead of a phone number. Twenty-plus years building in South Florida and more than 150 remodels and additions, every one permitted and inspected. On a street where deliveries and closings both run on narrow windows, a file that reads closed is worth more than a fast start.
permitting-compliance.scope_intro: Filed ahead of a remodel or inherited from an owner who never finished the paperwork, these five fronts decide how a Hillsboro Beach property reads on paper.

scope_items.name: Open permits, closed out
scope_items.desc: We pull the address history at Town Hall, establish what each open record still owes, and carry it through re-inspection, revision or a replacement permit.

scope_items.name: Work nobody ever filed
scope_items.desc: Enclosed porches, added baths, swapped glass and rebuilt docks brought back onto the record with as-built drawings, engineering and inspection against the code in force now.

scope_items.name: HVHZ and turtle-compliant products
scope_items.desc: Windows, doors and roofing matched to approvals valid inside the High-Velocity Hurricane Zone, with ocean elevations held to the town's light transmittance limit as well.

scope_items.name: Passing inspection first time
scope_items.desc: Each phase requested when the work is genuinely ready, with a supervisor on site to open what the inspector needs opened and keep the next trade moving.

scope_items.name: Structural report repairs
scope_items.desc: Concrete restoration, balcony and railing work, waterproofing and electrical corrections that come out of a building's structural report, permitted and inspected like any other job.

faqs.q: Title found an open permit and we close next month. Can it be cleared in time?
faqs.a: Often, and the clock starts the day you call, not the day the lender does. We pull the address file at the town's Building Department, read what each open record is missing, and sort it. Some want only the final inspection nobody called. Some need a revision or a letter from an engineer. Work done with no permit may need one after the fact, plus construction opened where an inspector can see it. Hillsboro Beach closes a permit by inspecting it, so plan in weeks, not phone calls.

faqs.q: Do I file with the Town of Hillsboro Beach or with Broward County?
faqs.a: With the town. Hillsboro Beach runs its own Building Department out of Town Hall on the Mile: it reviews plans, issues the permit and sends the inspector, with applications and contractor registration handled through its online permitting portal. Broward County's role is different and easy to misread. The Board of Rules and Appeals publishes the county's code amendments, certifies the officials and inspectors, and hears appeals, but nothing is filed there. Work in or over the Intracoastal is the exception: it adds county environmental licensing on its own track.

faqs.q: The seawall and dock were replaced before we bought, and nothing is in the file. Now what?
faqs.a: It gets legalized, which is more work than permitting it on time and far less than the credit a buyer will ask for at the table. We document what exists, bring in an engineer to certify what can be certified, apply to the town, and coordinate the Broward County environmental review that in-water work triggers, with state or federal approvals on larger scopes. Waterway work here arrives by barge and leaves no trace on A1A, which is exactly why it is the most common gap on this island.

faqs.q: Our oceanfront building has a structural inspection coming. Can PGX do the repairs?
faqs.a: Yes, once the report exists. Florida's milestone inspection and structural integrity reserve study requirements reach condominium and cooperative buildings of three habitable stories or more, which describes most of the buildings on this strip and none of the estate houses. Broward also runs its own building safety inspection program for older multi-family buildings, with one and two family homes exempt. The engineer or architect signing the report is retained by your association, not by us. The repair scope it produces is ours: concrete, balconies, railings, waterproofing, electrical.

faqs.q: How long does review take, and what does permitting add to the budget?
faqs.a: Weeks, not days, and the honest variable is how complete the first submittal is. Interior work with no structural change clears fastest. Sealed engineering, flood compliance or waterway review runs longer, because those approvals run in sequence, not side by side. Crossing the fifty percent substantial improvement threshold in a flood zone changes the design itself, which costs far more than any fee. Fees are set by the jurisdiction and scale with the value of the work, so we price them against your real scope rather than inventing a figure.

permitting-compliance.cta_sub: Send the address and whatever the lien search turned up. We pull the history, tell you where you stand, and put the fix in writing, in English o en español.
